notes.name: R3 / D2 Character range / verified build comparison
notes.text:
R3 / D2 Character range — visual comparison, 2026-10-29
Observed build: f86981922dc279501d3a06f67c26eabd007ed791. Content: character-creator (content/character.json), character-range (content/character-range.json), station-greeter, middlebury-station.
MATCHES: Separate original portrait (160×180 logical pixels) and map sprite (64×80), same palette and geometry as Components. Creator portrait is 320×360 desktop and 160×180 phone; map sprite stays 64×80. Completion uses 160×180 portrait. Eight named skin swatches; 52 named range controls; six groups; mobility, captions, visual cues, colorblind palettes, contrast and scale; independent optional identity choices. Voice/filter are visible labels only. Save/reload retains choices.
FRAMES: Creator 74:9838 / 74:9987; completion 53:3263 / 53:3271; modes 78:3672 / 78:3842 / 78:4012. Existing portrait/sprite/control studies retained. Reconciled centered previews and separate 44px name/pronoun inputs. Completion now shows portrait AND map sprite, Edit character, Give feedback and Back to platform, with desktop columns and phone stack.
DOCUMENTED DIFFERENCES: Native inputs/selects/checkboxes render taller than compact option-list studies, with browser focus/validation chrome. Build scrolls the document and keeps preview sticky; Figma uses scrollable fixed-height specimens. Build shows saved name/state; Figma samples Coils/medium copper and Rowan. Phone build checked at 390×844; frame is 390×720 and scrolls. Build has selected-swatch check/name and a thin phone preview divider. Browser font metrics, wrapping and vertical gaps differ slightly. Larger UI increases form controls to 24px while preview captions remain compact; Figma larger mode uses 24px specimen text. Three named colorblind palettes in build map to the shared colorblind design mode; exact palette values remain in D2/M2 Handoff.
PROTOTYPE: Existing platform→creator→completion→edit chain read back unchanged. Back to platform now returns to 38:2846 desktop / 38:3078 phone. Give feedback is a visual specimen in Figma; the local build opens feedback/index.html?demo=D2-character&version=<built SHA>. No external feedback URL or public deployment invented.
OBSERVED CHECKS: Compared desktop/phone creator and completion screenshots with the same Coils/medium copper character. No horizontal overflow. npm run validate passed: 27 tests, TypeScript, production build. npm run test:browser passed all 14 desktop/phone checks, including option pixels, access, persistence and D1 regressions. Native controls and scrolling differences above are intentional; no pixel-identical claim.
LOCAL DEMO: From repository run npm ci && npm run validate && npm run preview, then open the printed local URL. Platform → Create your character → Save → feedback/edit/return. This is D2 only. M3 remains held. No 3D engine, audio recording or prohibited wardrobe added.

notes.name: D3 escort — escort-arrival / welcome / station-greeter Saved walking, wheelchair, dialogue, route and endpoint frames retained. Accessibility studies 92:4723 / 92:4824 / 92:4925 retained; facing study 93:4921. Build: character creator → Walk with the greeter → station → Triangle Park → Arrival Green → first-year halls → hall → room. Graph exits govern transitions. Arrow/WASD and touch direction controls move on an integer grid; level route and stone collision apply equally to foot and wheelchair. Camera follows horizontally. Greeter follows saved movement history. Dialogue opens a separate portrait over the map; movement pauses. Differences: native buttons and browser focus chrome; saved character instead of design sample; dynamic viewport camera instead of prototype jump previews. Facing uses the existing layered character, mirrored west, rear face north, and a ground arrow. Map native 480×270 at 2× desktop; phone crops to 320×270 at 1×. Simplified buildings and fountain use original editable rectangles; decorative trees from the specimen are omitted in runtime. Captions and sample dialogue are text; no recorded audio. D3 ends at room, before unpacking. Existing notes, unlocks and identity remain saved. Town stays locked. Local: npm run validate && npm run preview. Give D3 feedback opens feedback/index.html?demo=D3-escort&version=<built SHA>. No public URL. M4 held. Tests cover foot and wheelchair welcome completion, collision, save round trip and desktop/phone journey including dialogue and reload.

notes.name: D4 — dorm-settle / dorm-room Frames 95:4981 / 95:4995 unpack; 95:5009 / 95:5026 finished notice. Entry 96:4981 from D3 endpoint. Original integer room geometry, bed and desk, three item positions. Build substitutes the player-selected origin for {origin}; book, mug and keepsake are generic belongings brought from that story location. No real-life inference or fabricated cultural detail. Native selects place each item into a unique slot; filled slots show B/M/K labels. Unpack precedes placement, finishing requires all three, and only then reveals the sample orientation notice. Positions and finished notice survive reload; old doodads and unrelated progress are preserved. Differences: native controls and focus chrome, item initials in room, document flow on small screens. Prototype jumps from unpack to finished specimen; actual build requires all three placements. D4 feedback opens existing local form with built SHA. Back returns to escort. Notice points downstairs but does not move the character or start orientation. No M5. Local: npm ci && npm run validate && npm run preview. Reach dorm on the escort, then Unpack in your room. No public deployment URL.

notes.name: D5 campus orientation — orientation quest; campus places and NPCs from content/ Frames: walk desktop 99:4982 / phone 99:5099; portrait dialogue 99:5216 / 99:5417. Dorm notice explicit start controls connect to these frames; conversation previews return to map. Prototype uses state jumps; runtime walks between graph portals. Player starts explicitly from the finished dorm notice, downstairs in your-hall. Walk to marked portals and interact to enter campus graph neighbors. Arrow/WASD and native direction buttons. Nearby text gives full portal/NPC names when the phone map crops labels. Talk near an NPC opens the more detailed original portrait and exact first bundled dialogue line, labeled sample; dialogue pauses movement and returns keyboard focus on close. Saved character sprite remains separate from portrait. Tasks: meet orientation leader, hall, Proctor, Davis Library, sample seminar room, introductory instructor line. The seminar has no lesson/notebook/ask panel: that is M6. Visited/talked facts persist so tasks do not expire or lose out-of-order visits. Town/outdoors exits excluded and town unlocks unchanged. Differences: native controls/focus styling, dynamic graph exits and nearby names instead of fixed sample labels; phone 320×270 camera crop versus desktop logical 480×270 at 2×. Bundled NPC text is longer than the short dialogue specimen; layout wraps in document flow. Simple map uses repeated original building geometry, sample geography, and actual saved player; prototype character/NPC samples are static. Local: npm ci && npm run validate && npm run preview. Finish dorm, Go downstairs for orientation. Give D5 feedback opens existing local form demo=D5-campus and built SHA. No public URL. Tests simulate orientation completion without downtown and desktop/phone walks with portraits and reload. M6 held.

notes.name: D6-class — sample-seminar-questions / seminar-room / fys-instructor Frames: class 103:5528 / 103:5655, notebook 103:5782 / 103:5787. Campus prototype links to class and notebook with return paths. BundleLessonSource implements LessonSource over content/lessons.json. Teacher paragraphs read only current lesson.blocks; selected answers read only current lesson.prompts.instructorResponse. Missing IDs refuse answers; missing blocks are application error chrome, not invented teacher speech. The sample is labeled the virtual lesson for this class. No live professor, network, LMS adapter or account. Player uses saved character sprite in the room. Teacher portrait is an original archetype, separate from map sprite. Previous/Next/Finish persist progress; completed state and asked prompt IDs save. Notebook saves notes with lesson/place IDs, accessible after leaving class. Missing notes migrate to an empty list; corrupt notes still fail validation. Orientation completion grants notebook, meal-plan and ask-a-question from quest rewards, also when loading older completed saves. Differences: native textarea/select controls, saved player replacing sample, desktop/phone document scrolling and native focus chrome. Compact prototype shows example question/answer; build waits for a selected lesson prompt and progresses one block at a time. No free-form answers. Preview text wraps with browser font metrics. Local: npm ci && npm run validate && npm run preview. Finish orientation, visit sample seminar, Attend sample virtual lesson. Open notebook remains available on campus. Give D6 feedback uses existing form demo=D6-class plus built SHA. No public URL. M7 held; the next cycle is meta, not executed in this pass.
